cards.explanation: The answer is earth. Shem, Ham and Japheth are the three sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated (Genesis 9:19). Three brothers, and the whole earth full of people! I once stamped one batch of cookies and needed a nap, friends. These three had a whole planet to fill.

The answer is vineyard. Noah, a man of the soil, plants one, and then he drinks some of its wine (Genesis 9:20-21). I know a thing or two about a batch going sideways. I once left a tray in the oven for one more minute. ONE minute. The text doesn't hide what happened next, and neither will I.

The answer is that he tells his two brothers outside. Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside. The text says nothing more about what was in his heart, so I won't guess. I think this is a hard moment, friends, so let's move through it carefully.

The answer is that they walk backward. Shem and Japheth take a garment, place it across their shoulders, and walk in backward to cover their father, with their faces turned away so they don't see his nakedness. Try carrying a garment across your shoulders while walking backward, friends. I'd have knocked over every mixing bowl in the bakery.

The answer is Canaan. Noah wakes up, learns what his youngest son had done, and says, "Cursed be Canaan!" Canaan is Ham's son, and the text doesn't tell us why Noah names him. So I won't guess at a reason.

The answer is True. Noah says, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!" and then, "May Canaan be the servant of Shem." The two sentences come back to back, friends. Verse 27 goes on to say, "…and may Canaan be his servant." and the text doesn't spell out whose servant that is.

The answer is that God may expand his territory. Noah says, "May God expand the territory of Japheth…" That's a wish for more room, and the words are "may God," so it's what Noah asks for. Every cookie sheet in my bakery is full, so I understand wishing for more space.
The answer is 350. After the flood, Noah lived 350 years. Add that up and the next verse gives his total: 950 years, and then he died. That's a lot of birthdays for one man, friends.
